handbookNote: South Carolina Code of Laws Title 26, Chapter 1 (Notaries Public Act, S.C. Code Sections 26-1-5 through 26-1-240 -- 26 operative sections; Section 26-1-70 is reserved and Section 26-1-95 was repealed/relocated to Section 26-1-160) and Chapter 2 (Electronic Notary Public Act, added by 2021 Act No. 85 (S.631), S.C. Code Sections 26-2-5 through 26-2-210 -- 22 sections), ~48 operative sections combined. Full statute text fetched directly from the South Carolina Legislature's official statute-publication site (scstatehouse.gov/code/t26c001.php and t26c002.php) and compiled at temp/handbooks/sc/notary.txt. CLASSIFICATION: South Carolina's BASE notary commission is APPLICATION-ONLY -- Section 26-1-15 (qualifications) lists only registered-voter status, English literacy, and a truthful application; there is no exam and no mandatory training/education course anywhere in that section or the rest of Chapter 1. IMPORTANT EXCEPTION -- DO NOT OMIT: Section 26-2-30 ("Required course of instruction and examination") is a real, codified, mandatory EXAM requirement: before performing any electronic notary act, an electronic notary public 'shall take a course of instruction of sufficient length to ensure that the electronic notary public understands his duties and responsibilities, as determined and approved by the Secretary of State, and shall pass an examination of this course,' covering 'notarial laws, procedures, technology, and ethics as they pertain to notarizations and electronic notarizations' (Section 26-2-30(A)-(B)). Section 26-2-20(C)(1) independently cross-references this exam, requiring proof of course/exam completion as part of the electronic-notary registration application. This exam applies ONLY to the optional electronic-notary registration/endorsement, never to the base paper-record commission -- so this product is framed as a self-study/reference practice-question set on South Carolina notary law generally, NOT general exam prep, with clear disclosure of this one real, narrow exam requirement via a distinctly-labeled supplemental topic file (electronic_notary_exam_prep.json, 20 questions) kept separable from the 10 other topic files (174 questions) covering definitions, commissioning/qualifications/endorsement, notarial powers/procedures, fees/certificates, status changes/resignation/death, unlawful acts/discipline/penalties, interstate recognition/Apostille, and the general electronic-notary provisions (definitions/registration, certificates/journal/security, discipline/recognition/scope limits). NOTABLE QUIRKS documented and tested throughout this track: (1) an unusually long TEN-YEAR commission term (Section 26-1-10) -- the longest scoped so far in this project's notary-track research, versus the 4-8 year terms typical of most states; (2) a distinctly POLITICAL/PATRONAGE-FLAVORED appointment gate -- South Carolina notary applications must be endorsed by the applicant's COUNTY LEGISLATIVE DELEGATION, either by one-half of its members or by the specific senator and representative in whose district the applicant resides (Section 26-1-20), with additional delegation-resolution flexibility under Section 26-1-25; (3) South Carolina's electronic notarization (Chapter 2) is IN-PERSON notarization of an electronic document (principal must appear in person before the electronic notary, Section 26-2-50(A)) -- it is NOT two-way-audio-video remote online notarization (RON); (4) escalated criminal penalties for electronic-notary unlawful acts (up to $5,000 fine / one year imprisonment under Section 26-2-150(B)) versus base Chapter 1 notary misdemeanors (up to $500 fine / thirty days under Section 26-1-160(H)); (5) Chapter 2 expressly does NOT apply to wills and trusts (Section 26-2-200) and does not override South Carolina's requirement that a licensed attorney supervise a real estate closing (Section 26-2-210). CONTENT DEPTH RATIONALE: 194 grounded MCQs were produced from the full 48-section, two-chapter statute text -- above this project's typical ~120-180 target range, but proportionate given South Carolina's Chapter 1 has an unusually dense central powers/procedures section (Section 26-1-90, subsections A through M covering acknowledgment mechanics, disqualifications, signature-by-mark, designee-signing, and unauthorized-practice-of-law limits) and Chapter 2 layers a full parallel electronic-notarization regime (registration, certificates, seals, journaling, system security, solution-provider registration, and discipline) on top of it; every question cites a specific Section 26-1-xx or Section 26-2-xx provision and no question was added merely to pad toward a target, consistent with the site owner's 'better nothing than nonsense' quality rule. PRICING RATIONALE: $0.75 (75 cents) reflects this project's lowest tier, appropriate for an application-only base-commission state whose real content depth (driven substantially by the unusually detailed electronic-notary chapter) does not change the fact that no graded exam or mandatory training course gates the base commission most South Carolina notaries hold -- consistent with this project's established pricing pattern for application-only/no-exam notary tracks (e.g., Kansas, Kentucky, Mississippi), each of which also carries a narrow, separately-disclosed electronic/online-notarization exam exception.
